text:
Miguel Santos: Heads up—support escalation from VertexWave. They opted into `cost_efficient` batching tier on their chat route yesterday and are seeing higher timeouts (client-side 30s) + some 504s. They rolled back to `standard` and it improved. I’m opening a thread here to coordinate. Ticket: SUP-18492.

Supportbot: SUP-18492 created by Miguel Santos • Priority: P1 • Customer: VertexWave • Summary: Increased timeouts after enabling cost_efficient batching tier • Link: https://jira.redwoodinference.internal/browse/SUP-18492

Miguel Santos: Initial details from the customer:
- Deployment: Hosted API
- Region: us-east-1
- Model: `rw-chat-13b` (their default)
- Workload: streaming chat (SSE), high concurrency spikes (they said ~200–400 concurrent during peak)
- Observed: p95 went from ~9–11s to ~18–25s, plus timeouts. Token cadence also felt “bursty”.

Miguel Santos: I asked for request IDs + a 15-min window + whether they’re pinning any explicit batching knobs. Waiting.

Aditya Rao: Thanks. This matches the known risk area for cost-efficient + streaming + high concurrency (queue delay / batch formation). Let’s get hard data: queue delay histograms, cancel/timeout rate, and overload reason codes if any.

Rafael Mendes: On-call SRE hat: if this is in beta ramp, we should treat as a rollback signal candidate depending on scope. Miguel—can you confirm whether they’re on the feature-flag rollout or explicitly set `batching_tier=cost_efficient` in config?

Miguel Santos: They explicitly set it in their route config (per their email). Not part of our default ramp.

Sofia Ivanova: For streaming, cost-efficient tier can increase `max_queue_delay_ms` to form larger prefill batches; that’s OK for non-streaming but can blow up “time to first token” and push end-to-end beyond client timeout.

Sofia Ivanova: Questions:
1) Are they using tool-calls / function calling? That tends to increase variance and can increase queueing.
2) Do they have long prompts (multi-turn) vs short?
3) Any evidence of overload protection tripping (shed) vs pure queue delay?

Miguel Santos: They do tool calling sometimes (RAG + tools), but they said the spike is on regular chat too. Prompts are mixed; they have some long “case history” contexts.

Sean Gallagher: From SLO perspective, cost-efficient tier isn’t intended for strict streaming UX unless they can tolerate higher TTFT and occasional p99 spikes. But we should still avoid *timeouts*.

Sean Gallagher: Miguel—ask what their client timeout is (30s you mentioned) and whether they’re setting server-side `timeout_ms` or `max_tokens` unusually high.

Nadia Rahman: If they share any `x-redwood-*` headers we can sanity check effective tier + any overrides. Also, do they have retries enabled? Retries + longer queue delay can amplify load.

Miguel Santos: Will do. For now I’m going to propose a workaround: switch back to `standard` for streaming routes, or keep `cost_efficient` but lower timeout sensitivity (or set a per-route override for queue delay). Need guidance on what override we want to recommend safely.

Omar El-Sayed: If we need a quick stopgap, recommend:
- `batching_tier=standard` for streaming
or
- keep `cost_efficient` but set `max_queue_delay_ms` cap (e.g., 8–12ms) and `max_batch_size` modest. The full cost-efficient defaults assume 20–30ms queue delay in some cases.

Sofia Ivanova: +1 but be careful recommending explicit knobs publicly; we should keep it simple. If we do give an override, phrase as “advanced” and include warning that it reduces savings.

Alex Martinez: Docs note: we currently say cost-efficient “best for offline/batch or latency-tolerant workloads.” Might need to add a callout: “not recommended for streaming UX with tight TTFT or low client timeouts.”

Rafael Mendes: Agree. Also: if they’re hitting 504s, that could be gateway timeout vs client. Check where the timeout occurs. If it’s our edge (or upstream), queue delay + prefill may push request past internal deadline.

Miguel Santos: Customer just replied with a couple request IDs + timeframe.
- Window: 2025-03-03 10:05–10:20 PT
- Request IDs: `req_01HR8T...9A`, `req_01HR8T...Q2`
- Client timeout: 30s
- They set only `batching_tier=cost_efficient` (no other explicit batching overrides)

Miguel Santos: They also attached a snippet from their app logs:
```
[10:11:32.104] POST /v1/chat.completions tier=cost_efficient stream=true
[10:12:02.221] error: ETIMEDOUT after 30000ms
[10:12:02.222] retrying attempt=2
[10:12:33.019] error: 504 from upstream
```

Rafael Mendes: That retry is concerning. Two overlapping long requests can worsen queueing. But still: we shouldn’t be pushing to 30s for typical chats.

Nadia Rahman: I can pull internal metrics by request ID if we have the trace lookup. Sofia/Omar—do we have a quick way to check queue delay and batch stats for specific request IDs in us-east-1?

Sofia Ivanova: Yes, tracing has `scheduler.queue_delay_ms` span attribute since last week (should be present). Nadia, if you have access, look for:
- `queue_delay_ms`
- `prefill_batch_size`
- `decode_batch_size`
- `time_to_first_token_ms`
- any `cancellation_reason`

Omar El-Sayed: Also check GPU memory pressure metrics—cost-efficient tier pushes harder on KV; if we’re near pressure thresholds, we can get stalls or more conservative scheduling.

Nadia Rahman: Pulled one trace sample (req_01HR8T...9A). Summary:
- stream=true
- TTFT ~14.8s
- queue delay p95 for this request ~22–28ms (sustained)
- prefill batch size: 28
- decode batch size: 10–14
- total latency to completion would have been ~38–45s (client timed out at 30s)
- no load-shed signal on this one (not rejected), just waited.

Nadia Rahman: Also seeing a concurrency spike on that model pool around that time (util high, queue depth increased).

Sean Gallagher: TTFT 14.8s is way too high for a streaming route unless they’re okay with it. This looks like queue-delay + large prefill batches under concurrency.

Sofia Ivanova: That’s consistent with cost-efficient tier behavior under load. The tier is doing what it was told (maximize throughput), but we need a guardrail for streaming to prevent TTFT runaway.

Rafael Mendes: Action: we should recommend they do NOT use cost-efficient tier for that route. If they want cost-efficient, use it on non-streaming / background summarization / embeddings.

Aditya Rao: Agree for customer guidance. Internally: this is exactly the product gap—we need workload-aware adjustments (streaming aware) even within tier.

Aditya Rao: Sofia/Omar—can we add a rule: if `stream=true`, cap queue delay and/or prioritize decode (or reduce prefill batch target) even in cost-efficient? Behind a flag is fine.

Sofia Ivanova: We already have an internal “streaming cadence fix” patch in flight for fast tier; we can generalize a guardrail:
- If stream=true: cap `max_queue_delay_ms` to X and increase decode priority.
- Also consider an admission control threshold so queue depth doesn’t grow unbounded.

Omar El-Sayed: For immediate mitigation, we can propose a server-side recommended override for streaming+cost-efficient: `effective_tier=cost_efficient_streaming_safe` (name TBD) but that’s a bigger product change.

Alex Martinez: From support POV, simplest: “Use standard for streaming. Cost-efficient is for batch/latency tolerant.” Then we can note upcoming improvements.

Miguel Santos: I’ll respond to VertexWave with:
1) Recommend reverting streaming route to `standard` tier.
2) If they want savings, use `cost_efficient` on non-streaming endpoints / offline jobs.
3) Reduce retries during peak or add jitter/backoff; retries are amplifying queueing.
4) Offer to hop on a 20-min call to map their routes to tiers.

Miguel Santos: Anything else we should include? Maybe a way for them to validate effective behavior (headers / dashboard)?

Nadia Rahman: Tell them to log `x-redwood-batching-tier` and `x-redwood-ttft-ms` if present (some accounts already get it), and to watch timeout/cancel rate. But keep it optional.

Sean Gallagher: Also advise setting a server-side max latency budget for streaming (if they have `request_timeout_ms` or similar) so they fail fast instead of hanging. But again, optional.

Rafael Mendes: Please also mention we can enable a temporary safeguard on our side if needed (per-account). If they insist on cost-efficient for streaming, we can set a cap on queue delay in their policy—let’s keep that as “we can do this with you” not a generic recommendation.

Aditya Rao: +1. Miguel, in your reply: ask them to share their route breakdown (streaming vs non, prompt length distribution) so we can recommend tiering per route. And we’ll follow up when we have the streaming-safe guardrail.

Miguel Santos: Got it. Sending response now.

Miguel Santos: Also filing an internal follow-up for the product team: “streaming TTFT guardrail in cost-efficient tier” referencing this incident. Linking SUP-18492.

Supportbot: Comment added to SUP-18492 by Miguel Santos • "Internal: traces show TTFT ~14.8s under cost_efficient + stream=true; queue_delay sustained 22–28ms; recommend standard for streaming; propose streaming-safe guardrail."
